chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Abu Ayoub from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding four who testified against a married man for adultery, two of them were considered just and the other two were not. He (peace be upon him) said: If they are four Muslims who are not known for false testimony, their testimony is accepted collectively and the legal penalty is established upon the one they testified against. It is upon them to testify with what they saw and knew, and it is upon the ruler to accept their testimony unless they are known for moral corruption.

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The fixed legal penalty prescribed by Sharia
key_terms.الْفِسْقِ: Moral corruption or deviance from religious norms
key_terms.مُحْصَنٍ: A married man or woman, specifically in the context of adultery penalties

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for accepting the testimony of four witnesses in adultery cases according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in cases of zina for a muhsan (married person), the testimony of four witnesses is accepted if they are not known for fusuq (moral corruption), even if their individual levels of justice (adalah) vary. It emphasizes that the primary requirement is their collective reliability and lack of known false testimony, rather than strict uniformity in their scholarly or moral standing, ensuring the hadd penalty is established based on what they directly witnessed.
